name: GRID3 NGA - Health Facilities v2.0
publisher: GRID3 (Geo-Referenced Infrastructure and Demographic Data for Development)
licence: to verify (not confirmed on the dataset page)
fields_used: state, lga, facility_name, facility_level, ownership, ownership_type, latitude, longitude, geocoordinates_source, last_updated
notes: GRID3 describes its facility data as non-exhaustive and non-validated. v3.0 (August 2026) covers only 24 states, so v2.0 is used for all 37 for consistency. 81% of coordinates are sourced from eHealth Africa (geocoordinates_source = GRID3_EHEALTH), so GRID3 v2.0 and the eHealth Africa dataset are not independent.

name: Nigeria: Health facilities
publisher: eHealth Africa (via the Humanitarian Data Exchange)
fields_used: name, type, functional_status, lga_name, state_name, timestamp
notes: Cross-check only. The file has no coordinates, so duplicates cannot be checked by distance.

name: GRID3 / WorldPop NGA population v3.0 (admin-level totals, scaled to UN projections)
notes: Modelled estimates (no census since 2006). Totals only: no age-sex groups in this file, so population aged 40+ is unknown for now. The mastergrid .tif in data/raw is not used.

name: Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey 2024 (NG2024DHS), state-level indicators
publisher: The DHS Program (ICF), National Population Commission, Federal Ministry of Health
licence: to verify (DHS Program terms of use)
fields_used: IndicatorId, Indicator, CharacteristicLabel, Value, DenominatorWeighted, DenominatorUnweighted
notes: The API returns no confidence intervals at state level.

name: Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey 2024, Final Report (FR395)
publisher: National Population Commission, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, ICF
notes: Blood pressure and blood sugar are self-reported ("ever told by a health worker"), not measured, and cover ages 15-49 only. They partly measure access to testing. Transcribed by pipeline/transcribe_ndhs_pdf.py into data/manual/ndhs2024_state.csv.

name: World Development Indicators (Nigeria)
notes: National only. Never spread across states.

name: geoBoundaries NGA ADM1 (state boundaries), simplified geometry, gbOpen release
publisher: geoBoundaries (William & Mary geoLab); boundaries originally from GRID3 Nigeria state boundaries
data_as_of: boundary year 2022; source updated 2023-02-26; geoBoundaries build 2023-12-12
licence: CC BY 4.0 (boundaryLicense field in the geoBoundaries API metadata; licence source data.grid3.org)
notes: 37 shapes. All 37 shapeName values join to data/lookups/states.csv (checked by pipeline/fetch_geoboundaries.py and tests); "Abuja Federal Capital Territory" shows as "FCT". Simplified geometry, for display only: not for measuring area or distance.

name: Monthly inflation and naira series, reused from the Money Matters project (naija-money-dashboard)
publisher: Central Bank of Nigeria (inflation feed GetAllInflationRates; exchange rates GetAllExchangeRates), cleaned by Money Matters
date_accessed: set by pipeline/fetch_monthly.py (copied from Money Matters' processed panel)
data_as_of: latest month in the panel (see meta.json)
fields_used: month, inflation, food_inflation, core_inflation, usd_ngn, price_index
notes: Same cleaning and caveats as Money Matters: June 2025 interpolated; 2025 inflation as revised by NBS in January 2026 (rebased series); naira rate is the CBN daily rate averaged by month, with one-day typos removed. price_index is rebuilt by Money Matters from year-on-year rates (an approximation, not NBS's published index). The health component of NBS CPI is not in this panel.

name: Consumer Price Index, monthly release (composite CPI, Table 2), National Bureau of Statistics
data_as_of: latest monthly release (see the release JSON in data/raw)
licence: none stated in the catalog metadata (rights field empty); cited as NBS
notes: Index levels, base 2024 = 100, January 2023 onward. From January 2025 NBS uses a new basket (COICOP 2018, health weight 6.06%); the 2023-2024 values are the old 2009-basket index rescaled by NBS, so the series is a splice of two baskets. The health index jumps about 10% in March 2025, just after the switch. Year-on-year rates here are computed from one workbook, and can differ from rates NBS published at the time (NBS revised the 2024 comparison values in December 2025).

name: Home page headline figures (hand-entered, one row per figure and source)
publisher: various (see data/manual/headline_figures.csv, one source and date per row)
licence: n/a (figures quoted from the sources listed per row)
fields_used: card, role, figure, unit, qualifier, label, line, source, source_date, url
notes: Every row verified against the source page on 2026-11-24 (verification_note column). Three figures rest on news reports of documents not yet found (NHA 2023-24, the World Bank programme document, the IARC 2025 assessment).
